proposal.title: Use LZ4HC blocks for smaller chunks with LZ4-speed reads
proposal.hypothesis: Operational evidence shows the consumer benchmark is warm-cache shuffled full-field tensor access, provider/cache changes cannot improve it, and Zarr metadata is 0.0% of measured output bytes, so the joint lever is data-chunk encoding. If the existing one-sample full-field chunks keep Blosc bitshuffle but switch from normal LZ4 to LZ4HC, chunk writes should use a higher-compression LZ4-family encoder while reads retain the same fast LZ4 block decoder path. This should reduce output_bytes and may improve consumer_samples_per_second by moving fewer compressed bytes per sample without changing array paths, dimensions, coordinates, selector paths, validation, provenance, rerun behavior, dependencies, or the public interface.
proposal.expected_tradeoffs: Materialization may take longer because LZ4HC spends more CPU while writing chunks. The semantic output remains lossless and interface-equivalent; the intended tradeoff is lower bytes and similar or better warm read throughput versus the current LZ4 setting.

edits.rationale: LZ4HC is a lossless Blosc codec variant that improves compression density while preserving the LZ4-family decode path for warm full-field reads.

proposal.validation_plan: Rerun the evaluator and confirm contract correctness, semantic equivalence, provenance/security, and rerun safety still pass. Compare the reported consumer_samples_per_second and output_bytes against the current node, while checking materialization_seconds only as an expected secondary tradeoff.
